references.text: Here it is mentioned that man was created in God's image, male and female, which reflects the creation account in Genesis 1:27.
This verse refers to human value as being created in God's image, an idea first introduced in Genesis 1:27.
The detailed description of human creation complements the overarching presentation in 1:27 that God created man.
The psalmist reflects on humanity's exalted position in creation, crowned with glory and honor, which is linked to mankind being created in God's image.
Expresses awe at how wonderfully God has created man, reflecting the creation of humanity in God's image.
Jesus quotes directly from Genesis 1:27 when he says that the Creator made them male and female from the beginning.
Paul refers to man as the image and glory of God, with a direct connection to the creation account in Genesis 1:27.
The new person is renewed according to the image of their Creator, pointing back to the original creation in God's image.
James warns against cursing people who are made in God's image, which points directly back to Genesis 1:27.
A direct retelling of the moment of creation confirming man and woman as God's image.
Jesus' direct quotation of the creation order as a basis for marriage theology.
Confirms and repeats the creation in God's likeness within a genealogical context.
Contrasts humanity's original righteous creation with its later sinful deviation.
